economic_justification: Broadest standard measure of real aggregate production and the natural quarterly growth target; connects to the growth discussion and to Okun-style output-labour relations. Real rather than nominal so price movements are not embedded in the output target.
statistical_justification: Officially observed quarterly; long postwar history from 1947Q1; no interpolation to monthly frequency.

candidate_series: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items
economic_justification: Long official monthly consumer-price series; inflation is central to Fisher, Phillips/Phelps and stabilization-policy reasoning.
statistical_justification: Monthly history from 1947M1, twelve years longer than PCEPI, preserving more postwar inflation regimes and business cycles.

economic_justification: Direct U.S. labour-market slack variable in Phillips/Phelps and Okun reasoning.
statistical_justification: Monthly, official, from 1948M1. Already a rate, so it is not logged; its level-versus-difference representation is set by the predeclared ADF/KPSS/ZA rule.

economic_justification: Monthly real-activity target needed to evaluate state dependence around recessions and turning points when GDP is observed only quarterly; strongly tied to cyclical fluctuations.
statistical_justification: Deliberately truncated to 1947M1 so that Great Depression and wartime institutional regimes, absent from the other targets, are not imported.
source_institution: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

economic_justification: Long monthly effective federal funds rate and the most direct policy-rate series for the thesis's Federal Reserve focus. Not replaced by a Treasury yield, which would introduce term-premium and maturity effects.
statistical_justification: Monthly from 1954M7; already a rate, so its representation is set by the stationarity and break rule.
source_institution: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

economic_justification: Gives empirical content to the money-supply dimension retained at Prof. Verne's request and supplies the monthly VAR with a monetary-conditions variable. Named the M2 monetary aggregate rather than 'broad money' because the official object is M2SL.
statistical_justification: Official monthly history begins 1959M1, which also fixes the VAR common sample.
source_institution: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

candidate_series: NBER based Recession Indicators for the United States
economic_justification: External chronology used only after forecasts are produced, to classify realized target dates into expansions, recessions, peaks and troughs.
statistical_justification: Not a forecast target and not a contemporaneous regressor, which prevents the official recession chronology from leaking future information into any model.
source_institution: NBER chronology distributed by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

exclusion_reason: Economically important and the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure, but it begins in 1959 and duplicates the inflation concept already represented by CPI. CPI is retained because it provides a longer postwar history from 1947 and keeps one inflation target rather than overweighting inflation in the cross-series comparison.
Alternative inflation measurement question, not necessary to answer the model-form question; robustness to measurement choice rather than a new element of the central research question.

Important to the policy motivation but not necessary to identify the model-form forecasting question; would introduce additional frequency, accounting and persistence issues and a separate fiscal-dynamics research problem.
Relevant for open-economy analysis but not required for the U.S.-aggregate core question; would broaden the thesis beyond the selected policy system.

Useful shock variable, but the previous Brent exercise remained a single-equation extension and did not resolve the multivariate criticism. Removed from the core design; restorable only as a clearly secondary application with explicit approval.
Would duplicate the policy-rate concept and introduce term-structure questions outside the core design.
Financial predictors rather than core macro aggregates in the approved Part 4 question.
